## Phase 2 — RED->GREEN complete; change up for review

**Gerrit change:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1481

### What changed (test-only diff; NO production code touched)

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py` — `test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` now
drives `/rerun` through `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` with a real `ReceiverConfig`, instead of
calling `rerun()` with a hand-rolled `types.SimpleNamespace`. `git status` shows exactly one
modified file; `git diff --stat src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` is empty.

Deliberately NOT done: bolting a `headers` attribute onto the SimpleNamespace. That would drift
again the next time the handler reads one more request attribute — and in fact the first attempt
at it proved the point immediately: with the real `GerritClient` constructed, the *config* double
failed the same way (`AttributeError: 'SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute
'gerrit_base_url'`). Using real contract objects makes the whole class impossible.

### Teeth proof — the test genuinely exercises its assertion, it does not merely stop erroring

Two defect-seeded mutations of the PRODUCTION path, each returning the corrected test to RED:

1. `app.py` 502 body changed to `{"status": "gerrit error", "detail": str(exc)}` ->
   **FAILED**: `assert {...} == {...}` / `Left contains 1 more item: {'detail': 'SEKRIT internal
   detail: /etc/passwd stacktrace'}`. The leak is named in the failure output.
2. `_request_token` header read stubbed to `""` -> **FAILED**: `401 Unauthorized` (proves the
   test actually reaches the 502 branch rather than passing vacuously).

Both mutations reverted; `app.py` restored byte-identical. The ORIGINAL test could not have
caught either — it raised before its first assert.

Refactoring litmus: the test asserts only observable HTTP output (status code, response body
bytes). It would not break under an internal rename.

### Verification

- `tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py` -> 20 passed (was 19 passed + 1 SKIPPED/ERROR)
- review-bot + opcert regression subset -> **156 passed**, 0 skipped, 0 failed
- 3x random-ordered reruns of the review-bot suites -> 117 passed each time (no `app.state`
  pollution across tests; `monkeypatch.setattr(..., raising=False)` restores it)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy src/rebar` -> Success, 436 files
- pre-commit gate passed on commit

### Sibling sweep (both axes)

- **Construct axis:** this was the ONLY hand-rolled ASGI request double in the repo. The two
  other `request = SimpleNamespace(...)` sites (`tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:589`,
  `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_verdict_provenance.py:223`) are rebar's own review-request
  domain objects (`repo_root`/`change_id`), not ASGI requests — not siblings.
- **Parity axis:** the rule is "an ASGI handler test must drive the real request contract". The
  other unguarded `request.headers` reader, `src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py:135`, is already
  tested exclusively through `TestClient` (`tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py:49,68,101,129`)
  — no MISSING slot. `/webhook` and `/rerun` in the 66af suite likewise.

### Residual risk — dispositioned

**Ticket filed:** `599e-77da-29dd-482d` (vampiric-dollfaced-aurochs), linked `discovered_from`
this bug — no CI lane installs the `reviewbot` extra, so every review-bot and opcert test
(including the security guards) is permanently SKIPPED in CI. That is how the 66af change earned
`Verified +1` while breaking this test, and it means this fix will ALSO be invisible to CI. Left
out of this bug's scope deliberately (it is a workflow change, not part of this root cause).

### Replication

The original report no longer reproduces: the exact command from the report now reports
`20 passed`, with the previously-unverified security assertion actually executing.
